item.title: Government criticised for failing to properly resource social housing audits in Longford
item.description: The Government has been criticised for failing to properly resource social housing audits in County Longford. It comes as figures show just 1.72% of social homes in the county have been audited by the local authority. In Westmeath the percentage is even lower at 1.31%. The data was released to Sinn Féin TD Thomas Gould and shows that just 70 homes in the constituency have been audited. Sinn Féin TD Sorca Clarke says it's unacceptable: Advertisement

item.description: The Bishop of Ardagh and Clonmacnoise has defended the decision to ban the practice of reposing in churches. item.title: Man hospitalised after crash between Carrick and Boyle
item.description: A man has been hospitalised after a two-car crash between Carrick-on-Shannon and Boyle. The vehicles collided on the N4 near the Cootehall turn at around 12.20 this afternoon. One person, a man, was brought to hospital as a precaution. Advertisement No one else was injured and the road has now been cleared.

item.title: Roscommon coroner pays glowing tribute to his late mother
item.description: A coroner paid a moving tribute to his mother at a sitting of Roscommon Coroner’s Court today. She died peacefully at the age of 96. Nancy O’Connor was a popular woman who lived on the Convent Road in Ballaghaderreen for many years. Advertisement She died in Galway University Hospital on January 25th. item.description: A Longford Councillor says the county needs more Gardaí. item.title: Longford man jailed for two years for assaulting train ticket inspector
item.description: A Longford man who assaulted an Irish Rail ticket inspector on a train at Connolly Station has been jailed for two years. Gerry Nevin (32) assaulted the injured party on board a Dublin to Sligo train at Connolly Station after the injured party asked him to leave the train because he had a can of alcohol.
